statement: Outside Book Dash, whose format fixes 12 spreads, 1 of 8 analysed books runs 12 pages (Chicken and Millipede, African Storybook); the others run 11 (Goodnight, Tinku!; Get Down, Rocky!), 13 (Good Night, Monu), 14 (Sweet Dreams), 15 (Bohlale's adventure), 17 (Kottavi Raja) and 18 (The Lost Ball). The 12-spread pattern is not shown beyond one publisher.

scope.population: contemporary open-licence picture books: Book Dash (35), African Storybook (2), StoryWeaver: Pratham Books (5), Room to Read (1); 2014-2026

analyst_note:
2026-10-14: Best Friends and An Unexpected Adventure (wordless) reviewed for this claim. Caution: all 7 are Book Dash, whose format fixes the spread count, so more Book Dash books do not answer the one-publisher objection; a second source is still required.
2026-10-15: Rewritten to the cross-publisher question the owner asked for. The 13 Book Dash books (all 12 spreads, a format rule) are no longer counted as support because they cannot test it. Word totals also split: the six 3-4 Book Dash books added today run 60-118 words (Zuko is wordless), below the earlier 136-220; non-Book Dash books run 168-569. Sources of the new works: Chicken and Millipede and Bohlale's adventure from African Storybook, Good Night, Monu from StoryWeaver. 2026-10-20: two more StoryWeaver/Pratham books, both off 12.
2026-10-28: two StoryWeaver books, both off 12: Get Down, Rocky! (Pratham, 11) and The Lost Ball (Room to Read, 18, the first Room to Read book). The 7 new Book Dash books all run 12 and are not counted (format rule). Sources of the new works: Book Dash — A Day Out, Who Ate My Hat, Let's Go Looking, Dudu's Hat, Clever Pig, A House for Mouse, Goldfish Genius; StoryWeaver — Get Down, Rocky! (Pratham Books), The Lost Ball (Room to Read, translated from Bangla).

magicpaper.suggested: Similar total length, but these books spend it on ~12 page turns of ~10-20 words. Worth testing shorter pages and more turns once the corpus is larger.
magicpaper.note: One publisher, one country. Do not act on this before ≥10 books from ≥2 sources agree.
